The decided functional scope of NoteDown, by area. This file describes the
current state of the concept: when a decision changes, the item is edited,
not appended to.

Each item says what NoteDown does (behavior terms) and, where it isn't
obvious, why. **Prototype** says whether the item is in `app/` yet
(round 1 = main view; round 2 = editor and dictation; round 3 =
multi-select; round 4 = sync and sharing; "app phase" = only possible in
the native app). **Open** names a question that blocks a decision. Items
without another source were decided with the user on 2026-10-13.

## Vision

NoteDown is a notes app in which every note is also a to-do: quick to
capture (typing or dictation), quick to tick off, and written as plain
Markdown that stays readable in any other editor once exported. On the
device only NoteDown reads the notes ("Notes and storage").

**Open** — who else it is for beyond the user's own use, and what sets it
apart from existing apps beyond the points above.

## Platforms

- **Android, iOS and web** are the target platforms of the app.
- The web app runs in desktop and mobile browsers, so all three device
  tiers in `PROJECT.md` → "Device tiers" stay in scope: phone and tablet
  through the native apps and the mobile web, desktop through the web app
  only.
- **A native desktop client** (Windows, macOS, Linux) is planned
  (backlog #58), with signed updates the user can check; until then the
  desktop browser covers that use. Why: a web app loads its code from the
  web host on every start, so whoever controls the host could serve code
  that reads the notes after decrypting them — the app is only as
  trustworthy as the host. Signal has no web client for this reason
  (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Security goal"). The web app stays as
  the convenient way in; the apps are the secure one.
- **Android and web ship first**, iOS follows (decided 2026-10-13: iOS
  needs an Apple developer account and signing, the first tests don't);
  the technology is in `PROJECT.md` → "Technology direction".

## Functional areas

### Notes and storage

- Every note is one Markdown section, and every note is a to-do: it is
  either **open** or **closed**.
- Each note has a **created** date, a **last-edited** date and an optional
  **due date**; a closed note also keeps the date it was closed. Times
  are stored in UTC and shown in each device's local time; a due date is
  a calendar day (so devices and members of a shared file in different
  time zones agree).
- All notes, open and closed, are kept as Markdown: one file for the
  user's own notes, plus one per set of people notes are shared with
  ("Sync and sharing"); the metadata sits in an invisible comment per
  note so an exported file stays clean in other editors
  (`docs/file-format.md`). *Prototype: round 1 (stored in browser
  storage; Copy and Export take notes out).*
- **Only NoteDown reads the notes on the device** (decided 2026-10-17,
  user decision, like Signal): the local files are app-private and
  encrypted at rest with a key the app can use but not read out — on
  Android and iOS from the platform's key store (hardware-backed where
  the device has it), in the web app a non-extractable WebCrypto key
  (weaker: it only keeps the data from being copied as files). Notes
  leave in plain text only by a step of the user: Copy, Share, Export,
  or an automatic export they switch on (backlog #55). Why: other apps,
  a lost unlocked file system or a cloud backup shouldn't read the
  notes. How (backlog #19, `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Where the files
  live"): one random data key per device encrypts everything NoteDown
  keeps — the notes files, the sync state, the settings, the file keys
  and the seeds of the device keys (backlog #61). *Prototype and app:
  2026-10-17.*
- Within a note, any Markdown is allowed, including further headings and
  task checkboxes; ticking a task checkbox doesn't close the note.
- An emptied note is deleted when editing ends, with Undo; a new note left
  empty is discarded silently. *Prototype: round 1.*
- **Local first:** every device keeps the complete notes on the device
  and works offline; in the app the files sit in the app's private
  storage, in the web app in browser storage, encrypted in both
  (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Where the files live"). *Prototype and
  app: 2026-10-17.*
- **Web app: notes only in this browser.** At start the web app asks the
  browser to keep its storage (`navigator.storage.persist()`), so it isn't
  evicted under storage pressure or, in Safari, after 7 days without a
  visit. While sync is off, a card above the open notes says they are
  stored only in this browser — clearing the site's data deletes them —
  with "Turn on sync" and "Export" (a card, not a strip or a line at the
  list's end: it risks data loss, so it should be seen). Hidden by the user
  (×, with Undo), it comes back after 14 days (a lasting risk that
  shouldn't nag). Not in the Android/iOS app, which keeps its data as app
  data, outside the system backup ("Privacy on the device"); a backup
  there is the encrypted backup ("Encrypted backup").
  *Prototype: round 1.*

### Privacy on the device

Decided 2026-10-17 (user decision, as Signal's apps; security goal in
`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Principles"). In the Android app; the web
app has none of these but the reminder setting — a stated exception: a
web app can't keep its window out of screenshots or steer the keyboard,
and a lock in front of a key that sits in the same browser profile would
only look safe.

- **Not in the system backup** (backlog #39): NoteDown keeps itself out
  of Android's cloud backup and of the device-to-device transfer of a new
  phone. Why: the local data is encrypted with a key that never leaves
  the device, so a copy is useless, and restoring the device keys would
  clone this device. Changing phones goes through sync (linking, the
  recovery key) or an encrypted backup ("Encrypted backup").
- **Screen lock** (backlog #6): Settings → Privacy → Screen lock, off by
  default. On, NoteDown asks for the phone's own screen lock — PIN,
  pattern, password or fingerprint — when it starts and when it comes
  back after being away for the chosen time: **Immediately** (the
  default), after 1, 5, 15 or 30 minutes or 1 hour. A share sheet or file
  picker NoteDown opened itself doesn't count as away. Turning it on asks
  for the screen lock once; without a screen lock on the phone it can't
  be turned on. Locked, a full-screen layer shows only "NoteDown is
  locked" and **Unlock**. It is a lock of the app, not of the data (as
  Signal's): the data key doesn't wait for the unlock, so due-date
  reminders still come.
- **Screen security** (backlog #59): on by default, a switch under
  Privacy. NoteDown doesn't show in the recent-apps preview and can't be
  screenshotted or recorded (`FLAG_SECURE`, from the first frame). Off,
  for a screenshot to share.
- **Incognito keyboard** (backlog #59): on by default, a switch under
  Privacy. Text fields ask the keyboard not to learn from what is typed
  (`IME_FLAG_NO_PERSONALIZED_LEARNING`; keyboards honour it, it can't be
  enforced). Dictation is not affected.
- **Speech recognition** (decided 2026-10-19): a choice under Privacy,
  **On this device** by default or **Online** ("Dictation").
- **Reminders without note text** (backlog #57): Settings → Reminders →
  **Show in reminders**: **Only the number** ("2 notes due today", the
  default) or **Note titles**, which says that titles show on the lock
  screen and that Android keeps a scheduled reminder's text unencrypted
  until it is due. Web and app alike.

*Prototype and app: 2026-10-17 (`?platform=android` shows the Android
settings and the lock screen in a browser, simulated).*

### Encrypted backup

Decided 2026-10-17 (backlog #56, user decision, as Signal's local
backups): with the local data encrypted and NoteDown out of the system
backup, a user without sync needs a way to a new device.

- Settings → Data → **Backup** → **Create backup** saves one file
  (`notedown-backup-2026-10-17.ndbackup`) with every note — private and
  shared, not the trash — and the settings, encrypted; on Android through
  the share sheet (Files, Drive, …), on the web as a download. By hand;
  the line under the row says when the last one was made on this device.
- **The backup key** opens it: 30 digits, created with the first backup
  and shown once (with "I have stored the backup key", like the recovery
  key), kept on the device for later backups. **New backup key** makes a
  new one; older backups still need the old key. Its own key rather than
  the recovery key: a user without sync has none, and the recovery key
  hands over the whole identity.
- **No keys inside:** no identity, device or file keys and no sync state,
  so restoring never links or clones a device.
- **Restore from a backup** (the same page, any device, sync on or off):
  pick the file, type the key; when the key opens the backup and this
  device has no backup key or a different one, a checkbox (on by
  default) offers "Keep this backup key for future backups": it is stored
  like a created key, so later backups use it and no new key is shown (a
  different one is replaced; backups made with it still need it). Same
  key: no offer. There is deliberately no "type my key" in Create backup:
  a mistyped key can't be checked without a backup file (backlog #62). It adds the backup's notes this device
  doesn't have — as private notes, since sharing belongs to an identity —
  and takes over the backup's settings (not the screen lock or the
  privacy switches). Nothing here is overwritten; with sync on, the
  restored notes go to the other devices like any new note.
- The file is PBKDF2-SHA256 (200,000 rounds, a random salt) from the key
  and AES-256-GCM over the compressed contents (`app/js/core/backup.js`).
- Not yet: an automatic backup into a folder (backlog #60).

*Prototype and app: 2026-10-17.*

### Sync and sharing

Detailed in `docs/sync-and-sharing.md`, the protocol in
`docs/server-api.md`; decided 2026-10-13, built in the app phase —
**milestone 1** is sync between the user's own devices, **milestone 2**
contacts and sharing (decided 2026-10-13, which halves what has to work
before the first live test).

- **Sync across devices** through NoteDown's own server, so notes written
  on the phone show up in the web app on the desktop. It runs
  automatically (after changes, on opening, on reconnect, and while
  open every 5 s, slowing to 30 s while nothing changes — backlog #21,
  to stay within the free tiers) with a status indicator.
- **End-to-end encrypted:** the server stores only encrypted files and
  never holds a key that decrypts them — notes are private by default,
  even from whoever runs the server. Files are padded to 4 KiB steps
  before encryption, so the server doesn't learn their exact size
  either (backlog #17), and compressed before that (decided 2026-10-15:
  Markdown shrinks to about a third, which saves server storage and the
  user's quota; app versions from before can't read such files). Keys
  are wrapped post-quantum hybrid (X25519 + ML-KEM-768, as Signal's
  PQXDH), so a recorded server database stays unreadable for a future
  quantum computer (backlog #20), and each wrapped key is signed by the
  device that made it, so not even the server can slip a device a key
  of its own (decided 2026-10-17).
- **Abuse protection without accounts** (backlog #8): the default server
  keeps at most **2 MB** of encrypted files per identity — thousands of
  notes; the user wants to raise it later as a paid option — and limits
  per IP address how often identities and linking slots are created
  (`docs/server-api.md` → "Limits"). Sync & sharing ends with a
  **Storage** bar ("0.4 MB of 2 MB used"; warning color from 80 %, red
  at 100 % with how to free space — archived notes count too), so the
  user sees the quota coming (user request 2026-10-14); hitting a limit
  also shows in the sync status ("Sync storage is full.", "Too many
  attempts. Try again later."). A shared file counts in full for every
  member, and an upload that would put any member over a limit is
  refused, so the bar shows what is enforced (backlog #27, over counting
  it only for its creator or splitting it); when someone else is over
  it, the status names them ("The sync storage of Lea is full, so this
  shared note can't sync."). *Prototype: 2026-10-14.*
- **Single notes can be shared** with other people. All notes shared with
  the same set of people live in one file for that set, encrypted so only
  its members can read it; sharing with one more person or removing one
  moves the note to the new set's file. All members are equal (edit,
  close, share further, remove, leave), and the whole note including its
  status is shared. Notes are shared with contacts; someone new gets an
  invitation link first.
- **Concurrent edits merge per note and per field;** when two devices
  changed the same note's text, their changes combine line by line —
  ticked tasks, counter steps (added up), stopwatches and added lines on
  both sides all survive — and only the same line changed differently on
  both keeps both versions (conflict copy), so nothing is lost (backlog
  #47; rules: `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Merging"). A concurrent edit
  of a note another member moved follows it only into the file the move
  names, so a member can't catch it with a note of the same id (backlog
  #32). A note with the id of one in another shared file stays a note of
  its own: notes are addressed by file and id, so both open, edit and
  share independently (backlog #63). *Prototype: `app/js/core/merge.js`, `app/js/core/text-merge.js`,
  used by real sync.*
- **No accounts** (decided over email login: simpler, and keys come from
  the other person instead of the server): turning on sync creates an
  anonymous identity with a **recovery key** shown once. Devices are
  linked by scanning a QR code on the new device; **contacts** are added
  by scanning their QR code in person or by an invitation link. The
  server knows no names or emails. The app works fully without sync.
- **Removing a lost device** from another one locks it out and renews the
  keys of every file it could read, so it can't read anything changed
  afterwards — without a new recovery key and without bothering contacts
  (decided 2026-10-13 over only blocking it or a new identity).
- **When sync stops on a device, a card above the notes says so** (user
  request 2026-10-16: nobody should type on a device and wonder why
  nothing syncs), in the look of the "only in this browser" card, which
  it replaces while it shows, in every view and tier:
  - **Removed** from another device: at its next sync round the device
    turns sync off by itself and keeps its notes, shared ones included,
    all private then. "This device was removed from sync — Changes you
    make here stay on this device only." with **Link again** (Sync &
    sharing → Link this device) and ✕.
  - **Sync data deleted** ("Deleting your sync data"): the same, "Your
    sync data was deleted" with **Turn on sync** and ✕.
  - **Blocked** by the server's owner: sync stays on and resumes when the
    block ends; "Sync is blocked by the server's owner until 25 Oct
    2026. — Changes you make here are kept and sync once the block
    ends.", no ✕ (it goes by itself).
  - **Outdated app** (backlog #51): the server no longer serves this app
    version (a later format or key change needs a current app,
    `docs/server-api.md` → "App versions"). Sync stays on, the notes and
    changes are kept; "Update NoteDown to keep syncing — This version is
    too old for the sync server. …" with **Reload** in the web app (which
    loads the current one) and "Install the current app" on Android, no
    ✕. It goes by itself with the first round after the update. Before,
    an outdated app just failed on data it couldn't read.
  *Prototype: 2026-10-16 (⋮ → Prototype → "Simulate device removal",
  "Simulate outdated app").*
- **Signing out this device** (backlog #15): Sync & sharing → "Sign out
  this device" takes the device off the device list by itself and erases
  everything NoteDown keeps on it (notes, settings, keys); the app then
  starts fresh — for a public or borrowed computer. It syncs first; if
  that fails (offline), "Erase without signing out" erases anyway, with
  the warning that unsynced changes are lost and the device stays listed
  until another one removes it. No new file key: a device that erases
  itself needs none, and one that may have been copied is removed from
  another device, which renews it. *Prototype: 2026-10-14.*
- **Deleting your sync data** (backlog #34, decided 2026-10-16, user
  request): Sync & sharing → "Delete sync data" (below "Your identity")
  and a page of its own at `<web app>/delete/` (no link from the app,
  no sign-in) delete the identity from the server. Both ask for the
  **recovery key** as the confirmation: it proves the notes are yours,
  and the page works without any device (all of them lost) — and app
  stores ask for both ways. Deleted: the notes, the device list, contacts
  and invitations; notes shared with others **stay with them**, the
  person shows there as "Tom (deleted)", with "Deleted their sync data"
  in the contact list, and can't be picked for new shares. Every device
  of the identity stops syncing at its next round and **keeps its notes**,
  shared ones included, all private then; a card above the notes and
  Sync & sharing say so, and sync can be turned on again as a new
  identity. Without the recovery key only the
  server's owner can delete it on request (admin page). *Prototype:
  2026-10-16 (`app/delete/?sample`).*
- **Version history** (backlog #7, decided 2026-10-15, user request):
  the server keeps older states of a file — one per hour for the last
  day, then one per day, for 30 days — and the user brings one back.
  - **An option per identity, not public yet:** while there is no way to
    pay, the server's owner switches it on on the admin page; a file
    keeps a history while one of its members has it, and every member
    of the file sees and restores it. Why: it costs server storage
    (whole encrypted copies; not counted against the quota) and is meant
    to become a paid option (backlog #33). Without it, nothing of it is
    shown.
  - **Restoring works on a whole file** — the private notes, or the
    notes of one circle — and brings back that state's notes (contacts
    and device names stay as they are now); for a shared file for
    everyone in it, after a confirmation that says so. The state it
    replaces stays in the history ("before a restore"), so a restore
    can be undone.
  - **Restoring a single note** (backlog #38, decided 2026-10-17): in a
    state's view every note under "Come back" and "Changed" has
    **Restore this note**. It replaces the note's current text with the
    state's (a deleted or trashed note comes back as an open note), with
    no confirmation, also in a shared file: "Note restored · Undo", and
    Undo puts back only that note, so edits synced meanwhile stay. It is
    written like an edit of the note, so it syncs to everyone in its
    file. *Prototype: 2026-10-17.*
  - **Where:** Sync & sharing → "Version history" → the file → its
    states, newest first, each with its time and a summary of what
    restoring it changes ("1 note back · 2 newer notes go · 1 changed").
    A state opens with what a restore changes — the notes that come
    back, the notes added since that go, the notes whose text goes back
    — and a "Restore this state" button (decided 2026-10-15 over showing
    the state's notes as they were: it answers which state is the right
    one and what a restore would lose). *Prototype: 2026-10-15.*
  - **Back up now** (decided 2026-10-16, user request): a second row
    under "Version history" in Sync & sharing, next to "Older states of
    your notes", saves the current state of every file with a history
    at once. Such a state is never thinned out, stays 30 days like the
    others and is marked "backed up" in the list; a file unchanged since
    its last backup adds none ("Already backed up: nothing changed since
    the last backup"). Why: a known-good state before a big change,
    without waiting for the hourly state. *Prototype: 2026-10-16.*
  - Older states stay readable after a device was removed (the renewed
    file key carries the previous one, `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` →
    "Version history").
- **Your identity** (decided 2026-10-15, user request): Sync & sharing
  ends with "Your identity", a page with the identity's ID in full and
  "Copy ID", so a user can tell the server's owner which identity to
  switch an option on for (version history, a larger storage limit).
  The ID is anonymous; contacts and the server know it anyway.
  *Prototype: 2026-10-15.*
- The server is built to scale to many users (stateless API, database,
  later an object store; `PROJECT.md` → "Technology direction").
- **Where it is operated** (decided 2026-10-13):
  - The top bar's **Sync & sharing** button (a cloud showing the sync
    status; under ⋮ when it doesn't fit) holds everything around sync: turning it on
    (name, then the recovery key, which has to be confirmed as stored),
    linking this device to an existing one (its QR code, or the recovery
    key), the devices (link a device by scanning, remove one) and the
    contacts (add by scanning or invitation link, show my code, remove).
  - **Sharing starts from multi-select** (long-press → Share), so one or
    several notes are shared at once; the share dialog lists the contacts
    with a checkbox each (a dash when only some of the selected notes are
    shared with that person), adds a contact on the spot, and offers
    **Leave** for notes of one shared file. Undo in the snackbar.
    **Group size:** a new group can have at most as many people as the
    server allows this identity (default 20, the user included; set by
    the server's owner, "Server maintenance (admin)"); once a note's
    group would grow past it, the unchecked contacts are greyed out and
    a line under the list says "A group can have at most N people, you
    included" (decided 2026-10-16, user request: the dialog prevents it
    instead of a server error). *Prototype: 2026-10-16 (the sample's
    limit is 3).* Chosen
    over a toolbar or a per-card button: it follows the existing
    long-press pattern and keeps the cards calm.
  - **Shared notes show their members as initials avatars** in the meta
    line (up to three, then "+n"), one stable color per contact; tapping
    them opens the share dialog. Chosen over a colored stripe or a list
    grouped by people: it says who reads along and keeps one sorted list.
  - **Sync status** is a cloud icon in the top bar (synced, syncing,
    offline), hidden while sync is off; tapping it opens Sync & sharing.
    A round that transferred something shows "syncing" (spinning arrows)
    for at least 0.8 s, then the check draws itself in the accent color
    and fades — a fast sync stays visible (decided 2026-10-13 over only
    spinning, which doesn't mark the end, and a pulsing cloud, too easy
    to miss).
  - **Syncing on request**, so the user can be sure to have the latest
    state: opening Sync & sharing (button or ⋮, every tier) syncs, its
    footer shows "Syncing…" and then when it last synced; on phone and
    tablet, **pull to refresh** on the list syncs too (decided
    2026-10-13 over a sync button: the icon already opens the panel).
  - Without sync, sharing explains that it needs sync and offers to turn
    it on. Notes in the archive aren't shared from there.
  - *Prototype: round 4. **Real sync** runs against the server:
    milestone 1 (2026-10-13) — turning it on, linking a device by QR
    code or with the recovery key, the device list and removing a
    device; milestone 2 (2026-10-14) — contacts by code or invitation
    link with confirmed requests, sharing notes, removing people and
    leaving, with the keys of every file renewed when a device is
    removed. The sample (`?sample`, `?sync=off`, ⋮ → Go offline)
    simulates all of it without a server.*
  - **Contact requests** (milestone 2, decided 2026-10-14): scanning a
    code or opening an invitation link sends a **request** ("Send
    request"); the contact shows "Waiting for confirmation" and can't be
    shared with yet. The one who showed the code or sent the link
    confirms: the request shows as a **card above the open notes**
    ("Mia wants to be your contact", Decline / Confirm, which asks for the
    name) until it is decided, and in Sync & sharing → "Contact
    requests"; on "My code" it opens at once. Chosen over a dialog that
    opens by itself (interrupts, and a link request often comes hours
    later) and a dot on the sync icon (easy to miss). Code and link work
    once (10 minutes / 7 days); on Android the link opens the app, and
    "Add contact" takes a pasted link. *Prototype: real; simulated in the
    sample (⋮ → "Simulate contact request").*
  - **Verified contacts** (backlog #4, decided 2026-10-14): a contact
    added by scanning their code in person is verified on both sides;
    one added by an invitation link (opened or pasted) is not, since a
    link is only as safe as the messenger it came through. Sharing with
    a contact who isn't verified stays possible: the contact list shows
    "Not verified" under the name, and the share dialog shows a notice
    with **Verify** below the list as soon as such a contact is checked
    (chosen over a label or an avatar badge in every row: the hint shows
    where it matters, the list stays calm). Tapping a contact opens
    **Verify contact** with two tabs: **Compare code** shows the safety
    code, the same 20 digits on both phones, to compare e.g. on a call
    ("Codes match" / "They differ", which advises removing and adding
    the contact again in person), and **Scan code** scans the contact's
    "My code" (chosen over one page with the code first: two equal ways,
    like Add contact). Scanning the code of an existing contact under
    Add contact verifies them too, instead of sending a new request.
    Each phone verifies for itself; the state syncs to the user's own
    devices. *Prototype: real; simulated in the sample (Tom).*
  - **Linking by QR code** (decided 2026-10-13): the new device shows its
    code under "Link this device", with the recovery key below as the way
    without a camera (e.g. two desktops). On a synced device, "Link a
    device" opens the camera; a scanned code asks **"Link ‹device name›?"**
    before anything changes (an accidentally scanned foreign code must
    not add a stranger's device), then the new device joins by itself.
    Scanning uses the camera in the browser and the Android app alike
    (one code path, no native plugin).
  - **Devices have names** (backlog #14): each device suggests one from
    its browser and system ("Chrome on Windows", "NoteDown app on
    Android"); it travels in the QR code and is kept, encrypted, in the
    private file, so every device lists the same names. Devices linked
    before names existed stay "Device n"; renaming is not built.
  - **Stale devices** (decided 2026-10-15, user request): the device list
    shows for every other device when it last synced ("Last synced 3 days
    ago"; "No sync reported yet" for one that hasn't reported a sync —
    always shown, not only with the warning, user request 2026-10-16). One that hasn't synced for **90 days** gets a warning in its
    row — "No sync for 104 days — remove it if you don't use it any more"
    — next to its remove button. Why: a forgotten device still holds keys
    and gets every new file key, and while it is listed the trash has to
    keep its purged markers for it (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Trash").
    The warning is in the list only, no notification. *Prototype:
    2026-10-15.*

### Server maintenance (admin)

Decided 2026-10-15 (user request): the owner of the default server needs
an overview for maintenance, a manual backup, and later a place to switch
paid features per user.

- **An admin page** at `<web app>/admin/` (no link from the app): an
  overview of what the server stores (identities, active devices, files
  and shared files, contact pairs, open invitations, database size
  against the hosting limit — a server setting, `DATABASE_LIMIT_MB`,
  since the database can't report it; an (i) next to "Database" says so
  on hover or tap, and while it isn't set the page shows "Limit not set"
  instead of the bar: the server still starts, user decision 2026-10-16),
  the identities with their storage use,
  devices, files and contacts, and backup / restore. *Prototype:
  `app/admin/` (`?sample`).*
- **Four sections, Overview / Identities / News / Backup** (decided 2026-10-15
  over one long page: scales to many identities and keeps the backup
  apart; News added the same day, "News from the server's owner"): on the desktop a rail on the left and the identities as list
  and detail side by side; on tablet and phone tabs under the header,
  the identities as a table (tablet) or cards (phone), and the detail as
  a page of its own with a back button. The list is sorted by last
  change, newest first; on the tablet its columns sort.
- **Only the owner gets in, without a password of its own:** the page
  signs in with the browser's linked NoteDown device (same origin as the
  web app, so it shares its keys), and the server answers the admin API
  only for identities listed in its configuration (`ADMIN_IDENTITIES`);
  for anyone else it doesn't exist (404). Removing the device ends its
  access. Why: no second secret to lose or leak, and the existing
  challenge sign-in is already the strongest one available.
- **No new metadata** (user decision): the page shows only what the
  server holds anyway — anonymous IDs, public keys, sizes, versions,
  times of change and who shares with whom; nothing like "last seen" is
  recorded for it. Devices appear by ID and kind, not by name (names live
  in the encrypted private file).
- **Finding an identity:** a search field above the identity list
  (every tier) filters it as the admin types any part of the ID — the
  short ID of a row or a full ID a user sent (decided 2026-10-15, user
  request).
- **Storage limit per identity:** the admin can raise or lower one
  identity's limit (default 2 MB) or reset it to the default; the app's
  storage bar shows the identity's own limit. Why: the first lever for a
  paid option, useful for testers right away; real payments are backlog
  #33.
- **Group size** (decided 2026-10-16, user request): the most people a
  new group (a shared file) can have, its creator included. The
  Overview has a "Group size" card for the whole server (default 20,
  2–50; 50 because every member's devices get the file key), and an
  identity's detail has one for the groups that identity creates, with
  "Reset to server-wide". The creator's limit counts when a group is
  created; a lower limit leaves existing groups as they are. Why per
  identity and not per group: a group's members are fixed, so a larger
  group is always a new group, created by someone. The app's share
  dialog knows the limit ("Sync and sharing"). *Prototype: 2026-10-16.*
- **Version history per identity** (decided 2026-10-15): a switch in the
  identity's detail turns it on or off ("Sync and sharing" → "Version
  history"); the list marks identities that have it with a "History"
  chip, the detail and the overview show how much the stored states take.
  Switching it off deletes the states of the files no member keeps a
  history for any more. *Prototype: 2026-10-15.*
- **Backup:** "Download backup" saves one file with everything the server
  stores (encrypted files, public keys, device lists, sharing); "Restore
  backup…" replaces the whole server state with such a file after the
  admin types RESTORE. A restore refuses a backup that would lock the
  admin's own device out. Devices notice the restore at their next sync
  and merge their notes into the restored files, so **nothing a device
  holds is lost** (notes deleted since the backup may come back, notes
  changed since then may show up twice as a conflict copy); a
  device linked after the backup has to be linked again. Hosting limits:
  a backup up to 32 MB can be restored through the page; the database
  host's own point-in-time restore covers the same case
  (`docs/operations.md`).
- **News:** the owner writes posts for everyone using the server
  ("News from the server's owner").
- **Blocking and deleting an identity** (backlog #34, decided 2026-10-16,
  user request; for abuse, test data and deletion requests): the
  identity's detail has an **Access** card. **Block…** asks "Until" a
  day or "Until I lift it"; its devices then can't sync and show "Sync
  is blocked by the server's owner until 25 Oct 2026." Nothing is
  deleted, whoever shares notes with it keeps syncing, and the block ends
  by itself on that day or with **Lift block**. The list marks it with a
  "Blocked" chip, the overview counts it. **Delete identity…** asks to
  type DELETE and deletes it like the user can ("Deleting your sync
  data"). The owner's own identity can be neither. Only whole identities,
  no single devices (user decision): a lost device is removed by its
  owner, which also renews the keys; blocking a device on the server
  alone would leave it what it has.

### Main view, archive and trash

- **First start:** the app holds only four short **welcome notes**
  (`app/welcome.md`, one per `## ` heading): what NoteDown is and what is
  good to know, how to operate it (tasks to tick), where the notes live
  and how they are protected, sync and sharing — onboarding with the
  app's own means instead of a tour (decided 2026-10-13; split into
  topics 2026-10-15 so each can be read and closed on its own). One text
  for every device tier ("tap or click", "Ctrl+click on a computer"), as
  the notes sync to the others. Linking a device drops the welcome notes
  never edited, open or closed. *Prototype: holds real notes from then
  on; the sample notes only with `?sample`.*
- The **main view** shows the open notes; the **archive** shows the
  closed ones. Both look alike; the archive has a clearly different
  background tint. *Prototype: round 1.*
- A note is closed with its own round check button in the bottom right
  corner of its card — distinct from the square task checkboxes inside
  the text. It moves to the archive, with "Note archived · Undo". The
  card's bottom bar is its only tool bar: the meta line (shared marker,
  due date, date) on the left, the round button on the right; the text above takes the card's full width
  (decided 2026-10-14 over a left column with the round button, which
  narrowed every note). *Prototype: round 1; bottom bar
  2026-10-14.*
- The **archive button** in the main view leads to the archive; in the
  archive the same button reads **Notes** and leads back, so one place
  switches between both views. It is an icon (tooltip) in the top bar
  right after Sync & sharing, before Due and ⋮
  (`docs/interaction-concept.md` → "Layout per tier"), and keeps its place
  in both views: the top bar keeps the same buttons in both. It carries no
  count: what was done today shows in the Due button's ring ("Due view").
  *Prototype: round 1; Notes button 2026-10-13; place and no count
  2026-10-18; top bar order 2026-10-19.* Why: a second
  "today" count next to the Due button read as overloaded, so the archive
  became the less important button.
- On phone and tablet, **swiping sideways** anywhere on the list
  switches between both views like pages: the archive lies to
  the right of the notes (swipe left to open it, right to go back); the
  other view moves in with the finger and the page snaps to whichever
  side it was let go past half (or flicked to). The contents list (the
  tablet's sidebar, the phone's open sheet) moves along the same way;
  the top bar and the contents' head stay in place and are only refilled
  (decided 2026-10-14: contents that jumped only at the end irritated).
  The title at the left of the top bar
  says where the user is. The view button stays as the visible way.
  *Prototype: 2026-10-14; pager behavior 2026-10-14 (swiping only worked
  on some tries and only switched after the gesture).*
- On the **contents panel** itself (tablet sidebar, phone sheet) the same
  swipe switches between its tabs **Contents | People | Labels** instead
  of the views, the same pager way; past the first or last tab it only
  gives a little (decided 2026-10-15, user request: the tabs are then a
  thumb's swipe away, the views stay on the list). *Prototype:
  2026-10-15.*
- Closed notes are **read-only**. In the archive, unchecking a note's
  round button reopens it (with Undo), and notes can be deleted
  (multi-select). *Prototype: reopen in round 1, delete in round 3.*
- **Empty archive** moves every closed note into the trash at once — the
  whole archive, whatever the search shows — after a confirmation that
  says how many go. Shared closed notes go only when the dialog's "Also
  delete … shared with others" is ticked, which warns that they go for
  everyone; Undo afterwards. It is the archive's floating button:
  entering the archive, the + moves to the bottom left and turns into a
  red bin (animated), set apart from + so the two aren't mixed up
  (decided 2026-10-15 over a ⋮ entry). *Prototype: 2026-10-14; bin
  button 2026-10-15.*
- **Permanent notes** (decided 2026-10-15, user request) are notes of
  lasting value, not tasks — a recipe, a list of book ideas. A permanent
  note has a mark (∞) in the round button's place, can't be closed and
  never goes to the archive; it is otherwise an open note (editing, due
  date, reminders). **Make permanent / Make closable** in the selection
  bar ("Multi-select") switches it. It is a **status of the note**
  (`docs/file-format.md`), so it holds for every member of a shared note
  and on all devices; a note merged from a permanent one is permanent.
  Why: it replaces the device-local protection from deletion, which had
  to be set in advance, didn't reach the user's other devices and was hard
  to explain; with the trash nothing is lost by a delete, and what is
  meant to last is now visibly marked as such. The mark alone, no colored
  card edge (decided 2026-10-15: permanent notes are rare, the mark is
  enough). A tap on the mark **filters the list to the permanent notes**,
  as a tap on a label does: a chip "∞ Permanent ×" above the list, next to
  the circles' and labels' chips, combined with them (it narrows them);
  not remembered across starts. The Labels tab lists the same filter as
  its first entry ("Labels"). Decided 2026-10-18 over the switch
  "Permanent first" in the sort menu, which competed with the Shelves'
  pile and shelves. *Prototype: 2026-10-15; filter 2026-10-18.*
- **Trash** (decided 2026-10-15, user request): **Delete** moves notes
  into the trash at once, with Undo (no confirmation, as nothing is
  lost). The trash keeps them for **30 days**, then they are gone for
  good. It is a view of its own like the archive — same layout, its own
  tint, a hint line on top, sorted by deletion date — and
  holds whatever disappeared from a file the user can see: the user's own
  deletes and the deletes of other members of a shared note
  (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Trash"). It lives in the user's
  **private file**, so every member has their own and nobody can empty
  another's. A note deleted from a shared file shows the circle's avatars
  **crossed out** and stays under that circle in the people filter.
  Trashed notes are read-only. **Every action acts on the selection** —
  there is no "empty trash" (decided 2026-10-15, user request): a tap
  selects a note, and the selection bar at the top offers **Restore**
  (a note from a shared file goes back to its circle, after a
  confirmation as it reaches others), **Restore as my own** (when a note
  from a shared file is selected) and Copy. **Delete permanently** sits
  far from those, as the trash's floating button — the archive's red bin
  at the bottom left, greyed out until notes are selected — and asks
  first, saying it can't be undone later (Undo for 5 seconds still
  follows). Why: restoring and destroying must not sit side by side. The
  trash is reached under **⋮ → Trash (n)** only, the view button leads back to
  the notes (decided 2026-10-15 over a button in the archive's top bar:
  deleted notes are rarely needed and get no permanent place). Once there,
  it behaves like a page right of the archive: swiping right or the
  Android back gesture goes to the archive; swiping left in the archive
  never reaches it (2026-10-15, user request: the way in stays deliberate,
  the way out is free). The 30 days count from when the
  user's first device notices the delete, not from the delete itself: a
  member who opens NoteDown after two months still finds the note in the
  trash for 30 days. A note removed for good stays gone even on a device
  that was offline meanwhile. Not in the trash: notes of a circle
  the user was removed from (the others' decision, not a delete), an
  emptied note (nothing to restore) and news posts (their own state).
  *Prototype: 2026-10-15.*
- The **+ button** sits at the bottom right of the main view. *Prototype:
  round 1.*
- Rendered notes show their **due date** as a chip: red when overdue,
  accent-colored when due today. In the archive the due date is shown
  without warning colors. *Prototype: round 1.*
- On an open note the chip is a button: a tap opens the **due-date menu**
  (today, tomorrow, in a week, pick a date, remove), without entering edit
  mode; a note without a due date shows an empty outlined chip "Due date"
  in its place. Archived notes show the date only (read-only). Why: the
  toolbar button alone was hard to find — only visible while editing and
  scrolled out of view on the phone. *Prototype: 2026-10-14.*
- **Reminders for due dates** (backlog #1): on a note's due day, at one
  time of day for all notes (default 09:00), one notification lists the
  open notes due that day — by their own due date or an open task's date
  ("Due date per task") — ("2 notes due today" and their titles); tapping
  it opens the **Due view** (below). Closed
  notes and notes without a due date never remind; no per-note times.
  Off until turned on under **Settings → Reminders** (a switch and the
  time), which is when the platform asks for notification permission;
  the due-date menu ends with a **Reminders…** link to that page.
  A **setting of this device**, not synced, since the permission is per
  device. The Android app schedules local notifications on the device, so
  they come while the app is closed; the web app reminds only while it is
  open — the browser can't wake a closed web app without server push —
  and the page says so. *Prototype: 2026-10-14; in the settings
  2026-10-16.* Why in the settings: it is set once, a top-bar bell
  took room for it all the time; offered only in the due-date menu it
  would read as per note, so the menu only links there.
- **Due view** (backlog #65, decided 2026-10-18): one place that lists
  everything due, item by item — every open note with its own due date
  and every open or in-progress task with a date ("Due date per task"),
  each as its own row; closed and deleted notes don't show, permanent
  ones do. Groups **Overdue**, **Today**, **Next 7 days** and **Later**
  (collapsed until tapped), each with its count; within a group by date.
  A note row has the note's round close button, its title and the date; a
  task row the task's checkbox, its text, "in" its note's title and the
  date (no date in Today; red when overdue). Ticking a task or closing a
  note works right there; the row stays in place, shown done, and can be
  undone until the view is left — rows never jump away under the finger.
  A tap on the rest of a row shows the note in the list. Empty: "Nothing
  is due." Opened from a **calendar icon in the top bar** whose corner
  shows how many items are overdue or due today (red when any is
  overdue), in every view, and by a tapped reminder. A green **ring**
  around the icon fills with what was **done today**: notes closed and
  tasks ticked today, planned or not, as done ÷ (done + still due now) —
  full once nothing is left, and at once on a day without plans; no ring
  on a day with neither (decided 2026-10-18 over a "done today" line in
  the Due view and a badge that turns into a check). Why: "I got
  something done today" and "what is still planned for today" in one
  place instead of two counts. It is a panel like
  the settings: a full-screen sheet on the phone, a centered dialog on
  tablet and desktop. Why: notes and their tasks carry dates, but the
  list shows notes — only an item-by-item list answers "what is due
  now"; a section above the list and a "due until today" filter were
  tried as mockups and not chosen. *Prototype: 2026-10-18.*

### Sorting and search

- Both views sort by **last edited**, **created**, **due date** or
  **alphabetically** (first heading, else first sentence); the archive
  additionally by **closed** date. Each option can be reversed. Defaults:
  last edited, newest first; in the archive closed, newest first.
  Notes without the sort value (no due date) always come last; by due
  date a note's open task dates count too ("Due date per task"). The choice
  is remembered per view. *Prototype: round 1.*
- **The sort button floats above the + button** (main view and archive; in
  the archive, where + turns into the bin at the left, it takes the
  corner): a small pill with an arrow for the direction (up ascending,
  down descending) and the sort's short name — "Edit", "New", "Due",
  "ABC", "Closed"; Shelves show a shelf icon and "Shelves", shared shelves
  "Shared". A tap opens the sort menu (sort and direction; with Shelves
  **Tidy up…** / **Arrange…**). It gives way while editing, selecting and
  recording, and isn't in the trash. On the phone the open contents sheet
  covers it, so the sheet carries the same pill above its level stepper.
  The top bar has no sort button. Decided 2026-10-19 (user request:
  switching the sort quickly is a core feature, arranging one tap
  further) over the pill beside or below the + and the top bar's button;
  the short label over the full name and direction, which took too much
  room. *Prototype: 2026-10-19.*
- **Shelves** (backlog #24) is one more sort option, in the main view
  and the archive: the user's own order — the core of the app, turning
  spontaneous notes into an order of one's own without asking for one when
  a note is written: notes are put onto shelves. Named "Shelves"
  (2026-10-19, user request, over "My order", itself chosen 2026-10-18
  over "Custom"; the picture of putting notes onto shelves says what it
  does). Notes start on the **Pile**: the
  notes not sorted in yet, **first in the list** under a tinted header
  "Pile" with their count and **Tidy up…**, by last edited, newest first;
  then the sorted notes (decided 2026-10-18 over the pile at the end: a new
  note appears where the user looks, as in every other sort, and folding
  keeps the order in view). A tap on the header **folds** the pile to that
  one line, remembered per device like a section; a search shows it
  unfolded. A new note lands on top of the pile at once, also when it was
  empty, and shows there even with the pile folded (user request
  2026-10-19: an empty pile's header stayed below it). With the pile empty
  the header reads "Pile empty" with a check and the link **Arrange…**
  (user request 2026-10-19: re-arranging a fully sorted order from the
  list and the contents). The sort menu's **Tidy up…** — **Arrange…** with
  the pile empty — (and the same link on
  the header in the list and in the table of contents) opens a dialog like
  the merge order dialog, where notes move above a line by drag (or arrow
  keys) or with + / −, and are ordered there; the pile is below the line.
  Each note row's move button moves the note into a section of another
  (Multi-select → "Move to").
  Shelves have no direction. The dialog arranges what the list shows
  (circle filter and search applied); other notes keep their places in the
  order. Below the list, "Pile by …" sorts the pile's rows with any sort
  but the custom ones, both directions (last edited, newest first, at
  first), so the next notes to sort in are easy to find; the control sits
  under the list so nothing but the line stands between the rows
  (decided 2026-10-15). Save
  offers Undo. There is one such order only (several named orders go
  too far for now). It is **synced but private**: one marker in the
  private file lists the note ids (`docs/file-format.md`), so shared notes
  can be ordered too without the other members seeing it; when two devices
  changed it, the newer list wins. *Prototype: 2026-10-14; named, pile on
  top 2026-10-18.*
- **Tidy-up reminder** (decided 2026-10-18, user request; reworked the
  same day into bars): the pile header shows how full the pile is as a
  gauge of **bars**. One bar fills per *n* notes on the pile and one per
  *d* days its oldest note has waited, both in whole steps and added up
  (3 notes at 2 per bar and 11 days at 5 per bar fill 1 + 2 bars); more
  than fit show the gauge full. Filled bars are grey, **yellow** from 75 %
  but at the latest one bar before full, with "Tidy up"; **red** when
  full, with "Time to tidy up" and a dot on the sort button, whatever the
  list is sorted by.
  **Settings → Tidy-up reminder** sets the three numbers for every circle
  alike, each with − / +: Bars (1–10, default 5), Notes per bar (1–20,
  default 2), Days per bar (1–30, default 2) — about the old "10 notes or
  a week" when either acts alone. Below, each circle (Private, each
  contact, each group) is **counted or ignored** by a switch; **Private
  counted by default, shared circles ignored** (others often sort shared
  notes). An ignored circle's view shows no gauge, and where several
  circles show together only the counted circles' notes are taken
  together. Main view only; a setting of this device. A gauge rather than
  a score or push messages: it should invite tidying, never make it a
  chore. *Prototype: 2026-10-18.*
- **A shelf** in Shelves (and in shared shelves), called a section until
  2026-10-19: the arrange dialog's **+ Shelf** adds a named divider right
  above the pile's line; it moves like a note, its name is edited in place
  and its × removes it (its notes stay where they are and join the shelf
  above). A shelf holds the sorted notes below it up to the next one; it
  is no note (no body, no status, not exported) and exists only above the
  line. In the list and the table of contents (as the top level there)
  each shelf heads its notes with a title line and their count; a tap
  folds or unfolds it, remembered per device; a search shows every shelf
  unfolded, so all hits show. A shelf without notes in the current view
  isn't shown. Stored as entries in the order's id list
  (`docs/file-format.md`). *Prototype: 2026-10-18 (user request; the
  title-line look chosen over a grouping box and a sticky band, as the
  lightest one beside the pile's header).*
- **Shared shelves** (backlog #25, "Shared order" until 2026-10-19): in
  the view of a circle with people ("People circles as a filter") the sort
  menu also offers "Shared shelves" — an order of that circle's notes kept
  in the circle's own file, so every member sees and edits the same one;
  any member may set it, none has to. It works like Shelves (Tidy up…, the pile with its reminder unless that circle is ignored, Undo; the
  dialog says who sees it) and merges the same way, the newer list
  winning. Outside a circle's view a view set to it shows the user's own
  Shelves. *Prototype: 2026-10-14; real on shared files since
  milestone 2, simulated in the sample (Lea's circle carries one).*
- When an edit ends, the note **sorts in at once**: it stays where it is
  on the screen and the list moves around it, as far as the scroll range
  allows; the table of contents always shows the list's order (decided
  2026-10-19: a list that kept its old order while the contents re-sorted
  looked unreliable). While a note is edited the list keeps its order.
  Sorted by due date, a new due date sorts its note in the same way even
  while it is edited (decided 2026-10-15: the user wants to see where it
  lands). *Prototype: 2026-10-19.*
- A note that **no longer matches the filters** when its edit ends (a
  label filter, permanent only) folds away with a short animation and
  "Note hidden by the filter", so its disappearing can be followed
  (user request 2026-10-19). *Prototype: 2026-10-19.*
- A **full-text search** in the top bar filters the current view; the
  table of contents follows the filter. *Prototype: round 1.*
- Where the search text occurs it is **highlighted** in the notes and in
  the contents entries (also across formatting), so the place of a hit
  shows, not only its note (decided 2026-10-15). The note being edited
  shows no highlight (its editor shows the plain text); it returns when
  editing ends. The search field shows a **counter** "current/total" of
  the hits in the notes and **▲ / ▼** that step to the previous / next
  hit (Enter / Shift+Enter in the field), wrapping around at the ends:
  the current hit is marked more strongly and scrolled into the middle of
  the screen. A new search text starts at its first hit, scrolled to when
  it is out of view. *Prototype: 2026-10-15.*
- **Ending the search keeps the place** (user request 2026-10-18, found
  on Android): ×, the back key or `Esc` end it, and the note with the
  current hit — scrolled away from it, the topmost note in view — stays
  where it is on the screen while the other notes come back around it,
  and flashes; a folded shelf or pile holding it unfolds. Back ends the
  search once a text is typed (on the phone: once the field is open).
  *Prototype: 2026-10-18.*
- The search field **suggests** (backlog #66, user idea 2026-10-18): a
  tap into the empty field offers the filters — "∞ Permanent", every
  label and every circle (contacts, groups, Private), each with its count;
  `#` offers only the labels. Typing narrows them and adds the **headings**
  that match. Matching is **fuzzy**: the typed letters in order with gaps
  ("trvl" finds #travel, "gp" Garden plan), ignoring case and accents, but
  loose letters count only as a word's initials or, from three letters on,
  with two of them together (fewer only match nearly everything). Picking a
  filter sets it as a chip above the list (added to the filters already
  picked, which are no longer offered) and empties the field; picking a
  heading puts its text into the search. The full-text search keeps
  filtering the list meanwhile, and itself stays exact, so its hits and
  ▲ / ▼ stay unambiguous. Desktop: ↓ / ↑ and Enter pick, `Esc` closes the
  suggestions. The People and Labels tabs stay: they give the overview with
  counts and picking several; the field is the quick way in. Shown as a
  list under the field with the kind and count per row — chosen
  2026-10-18 over a row of chips under the top bar, which hid kind and
  count and cut long headings. *Prototype: 2026-10-18.*

### Table of contents

- A table of contents over all notes of the current view, in the current
  sort order and search filter. *Prototype: round 1.* Sorted by
  Shelves, it shows the pile's header with its gauge and **Tidy up…** on
  top, folding with the list's (on the phone the link closes the sheet),
  then the shelves. *Prototype: 2026-10-17 (user request: arranging is
  reachable from the contents too); pile on top 2026-10-18.*
- Levels count from the highest heading level that actually occurs; it
  starts with **2 levels** and **− / +** remove or add levels (between 1
  and the deepest level present). The level count is remembered. The
  − / + stepper floats at the contents' bottom right, at the height of the
  + button (decided 2026-10-15, user request: within the thumb's reach);
  on the phone it takes the + button's place while the sheet is open.
  Beside − / + a switch shows the task progress ("Task states and
  progress").
- Text without a heading — a note without one, or the start of a note
  before its first heading — appears with its first sentence (shortened,
  italic) **one level below the last heading above it**, in whichever note
  that is (top level when there is none), so a note that belongs under a
  section shows there. A note boundary always ends a section.
- Tapping an entry scrolls to that place in the note and briefly
  highlights the note. A long-press on an entry selects sections
  ("Multi-select"); not in the archive.
- On the phone it is a **bottom sheet** whose **handle always peeks out at
  the bottom** — within thumb reach, and the handle shows where it is
  (decided 2026-10-13 over a side drawer; 2026-10-14 the handle replaced
  the top bar's contents button). A tap on the handle opens it fully (up
  to the top bar) or closes it. The sheet is one surface that moves as a
  whole: a vertical drag anywhere on it (closed: on the handle) moves
  it and leaves it at any height; dragged past the top bar it slides
  out at the top, which is how longer contents scroll (decided
  2026-10-15: opening and scrolling are one gesture, so it can also be
  pushed back down from anywhere). An upward flick that starts with the
  sheet closed (on the handle or an edge strip) opens it fully, like a
  tap on the handle (decided 2026-10-15: opening in one gesture); on the
  open sheet it glides on. A flick down closes it from anywhere, so does
  a drag below ~15 %. Closed, a drag up from a thin strip at either
  screen edge in the bottom third pulls it up as well (decided
  2026-10-15: the handle is a small target); there a drag down still
  scrolls the list. The height is not
  remembered. While editing and recording the handle
  gives way. Tablet and desktop show it as a fixed sidebar.

### People circles as a filter

- Next to the table of contents a **People** overview lists the circles
  the user shares with (backlog #23): **All notes** and **Private** on
  top, then the user's **folder sources** A–Z ("Folder sources"), then
  every contact A–Z — each entry is only the circle of that one
  person, also a contact nothing is shared with yet — then every group
  (a circle of several, named by its members, A–Z). Each entry shows how
  many of its notes the current view holds. *Prototype: 2026-10-14.*
- Tapping an entry **filters the list** to that circle's notes; archive,
  search and sort apply on top, and the table of contents follows.
- **Several circles** can be shown at once (user request 2026-10-16): a
  **long-press** on an entry (desktop: right-click or Ctrl/Cmd+click)
  starts picking several, as on notes — the tab shows a bar with **×**
  and "2 selected", every entry a checkbox, and a tap then adds or
  removes an entry (the phone sheet stays open). ×, the back key, `Esc`
  or taking out the last entry end it; the picked circles stay. The list
  shows the notes of all picked circles. News are only shown on their
  own; All notes clears the filter. Chosen over a tap that always adds
  (one more step for the common single pick) and a checkbox on every row
  (clutter): the long-press is how multi-select starts everywhere else.
- Each picked circle shows as a **chip with ×** above the list, which
  takes it out; with more than one chip (circles and labels together) a
  **×** in front of them clears all filters. The filter is not
  remembered across starts (it starts at All).
- **+** (and dictation) in a list filtered to one circle creates the note
  **in that circle** — for a contact without shared notes this starts the
  circle (each circle is one file, `docs/sync-and-sharing.md`). Without a
  filter, or under Private, a new note is private. With **several
  circles**, + first asks which of them the note goes to (a menu of the
  picked circles), and holding + doesn't record but says "To dictate,
  show one circle only" — a dictated note has no moment to ask.
- A **contact's page** (Sync & sharing → the contact) lists the **groups**
  they are in; tapping one shows that group's notes (user request
  2026-10-16; it replaces the long-press menu on a contact, which now
  starts picking several).
- Placement: **tabs "Contents | People"** at the top of the sidebar
  (tablet, desktop) and of the bottom sheet (phone) — decided 2026-10-14
  over a second section below the contents (both lists get cramped) and a
  separate phone sheet (one more top-bar icon on a full bar). The tabs
  **always show**, also with sync off and without contacts: then People
  holds All notes, Private, a hint "No contacts yet" and **Add contact**
  (opens Sync & sharing) — decided 2026-10-15 so the feature is there
  to be found.

### Labels

Decided 2026-10-15 (user request, together with the Google Keep import,
whose labels need a place).

- A label is a **#hashtag in the note's text** (`#travel`, `#home/garden`),
  as in Obsidian: plain Markdown that other editors show, typed like any
  text, no file format change (chosen over a hidden marker attribute,
  which needs its own UI and is invisible elsewhere). It follows a space
  or the line start and holds a letter or an **emoji** (`#😉`, `#🎂`,
  `#trip✈️`; skin tones, flags and joined emoji count as one — user
  request 2026-10-17); `# Heading`, `issue#5`, `#5` and the keycap `#️⃣`
  are none, nor anything in code or links. Labels compare case-insensitively.
- Labels are part of the text, so everyone a note is shared with sees
  them; there are no private labels on shared notes.
- In a note a label shows as a small **chip**; tapping it **filters the
  list** to the notes with that label. Circle filter, archive, search
  and sort apply on top; the table of contents follows. Each picked
  label shows as a **chip with ×** above the list, next to the circles'
  chips; the filter is not remembered across starts.
- A third tab **"Contents | People | Labels"** lists every label of the
  current view (circle filter and search applied) A–Z with its count; in
  the main view **"∞ Permanent"** with the count of permanent notes heads
  the list, set off by a line — a tap shows the permanent notes only,
  again all ("Permanent notes");
  tapping one filters, tapping it again clears it. Several labels are
  picked like several circles (long-press, "People circles as a
  filter"); a note then shows when it carries **any** of them (decided
  2026-10-16: the same rule as for circles). Labels don't affect where
  + puts a note. Without labels the tab says how to add one. Chosen 2026-10-15 over a row of label chips above
  the list: many labels (after an import) fit a list, and it works like
  the people filter. The three tabs take the head's full width.
- While a note is edited its labels show as plain text. *Prototype:
  2026-10-15.*

### News from the server's owner

Decided 2026-10-15 (user request): the server's owner needs a curated
channel to everyone — changelogs, information, a call to take part in a
poll — that only the owner writes. Chosen over read-only roles in shared
circles and over channels of their own: those change the sharing model,
this needs none of it.

- **Written on the admin page** (section News): posts look and are
  written like notes (the same editor), several at a time, newest first.
  Unlike a note, a post is only published or saved with **Publish** /
  **Save** (Cancel discards), so nobody reads half-written text.
  **Archive** takes a post out of the feed and keeps it on the admin page
  (**Publish again** brings it back); **Delete** removes it. Either way
  it is gone for everyone, also for those who had read it. At most 20
  posts are published at a time (`docs/server-api.md` → "Limits").
- **Unencrypted:** the server serves the published posts to every
  identity as they are — official communication, the same for everyone,
  so there is nothing to keep from the server and no key to hand out.
  The app fetches them in a sync round only when the server reports a
  new version.
- **In the app** they appear only while sync is on (without sync the app
  talks to no server), as **News** pinned at the top of the people
  overview, above All notes. Picking it lists the posts
  as **read-only notes** (no editing, no due date), newest first; they
  appear nowhere else (not under All notes). A post can be **closed**
  into the archive (round button, Undo) and reopened there, copied, and
  **deleted** for this user (multi-select → Delete, with Undo; no trash);
  closed or deleted, it stays so on all the user's devices and comes
  back only when the owner edits it — then marked as updated. + from the
  news starts a note under All notes.
- **New and updated posts are marked:** a label **New** or **Updated**
  as a chip in the card's meta line, and a badge with their number on
  the News entry, the People tab and (phone) the closed contents sheet
  (decided 2026-10-15 over a dot, which doesn't say how much is new, and
  a tag at the card's corner, which sits on the card's edge). A post counts as
  seen once its card was in view and the user leaves the news (another
  filter, the archive, or the app goes to the background), or at once
  when the card is tapped, closed or deleted — so the label stays while
  it is read. Seen is **per user**, synced across the user's devices.
- **What the user did is private:** which posts were seen, closed or
  deleted is kept in the encrypted private file
  (`docs/file-format.md` → "News"), one marker per post that is still in
  the feed; markers of posts that left the feed are dropped, so the
  file doesn't grow with old news.
- *Prototype: 2026-10-15 — the sample shows three posts (one new, one
  updated, one closed) from `app/sample/news.md`; real sync fetches the
  server's feed.*

### Folder sources

Decided 2026-10-19 (user request: get the voice notes of the Index 01
ring, which the Pebble app writes as files, into NoteDown without a
server or a cloud in between). Built generally, for any app that writes
notes into a folder.

- A **folder source** is a named folder on an Android device that another
  app writes notes into, one file each — e.g. the Pebble app's Obsidian
  connection in "one file per note" mode. The name is free ("Pebble").
- **Settings → Data → Folder sources** lists them; **Add folder source**
  (Android app) asks for the name, then opens the system's folder picker.
  A source's page renames it, chooses another folder and **Remove
  source** (confirmed; the notes read from it stay as private notes).
  The sources and their names are synced (private file); which folder a
  source reads is a **setting of this device**, so the web app and the
  desktop show the sources but read no folder ("Read by the Android
  app"). When the folder's access is gone, the page says so and the
  folder is chosen again.
- **Reading:** the Android app reads every folder of its sources when it
  starts, when it comes back to the front and every 5 minutes while it is
  open. Each Markdown or text file directly in the folder becomes a
  **private note** (no heading, like a dictated note — sorted later), a
  YAML front matter block is dropped and its `created` time becomes the
  note's (else the file's time). Then the file is **deleted** (user
  decision: the folder stays empty; a file that can't be deleted is
  remembered and not read twice). A snackbar says "Note added from
  Pebble". Files over 1 MB and subfolders are left alone.
- **In the People overview** each source is an entry with a folder icon
  after Private, filtering to the notes read from it; they also show
  under All notes and Private (user decision: ordinary private notes, the
  source is a filter). It combines with other entries like a circle; +
  from a source starts a private note under All notes.
- **No storage permission:** the folder is reached through the system's
  folder picker, which grants access to that folder only (read and
  write, to delete what was read), kept across restarts.
- Reading while the app is closed is a separate step (backlog #68).
- Tiers: the People entry and the settings show on every tier; reading a
  folder is Android-only (phone and tablet), as only there another app
  writes files NoteDown can reach. *Prototype and app: 2026-10-19
  (`?platform=android` simulates a folder holding the sample transcript).*

### Creating and editing

- A **new note** starts empty in edit mode (no heading preset; the
  heading button adds one); it stays at the top of the list until editing
  ends, also when the filters would leave it out (user request
  2026-10-19: under a label filter it opened hidden and stayed behind
  empty). An edited new note sorts in when editing ends; a dictated or
  merged one shown at the top takes its sorted place with the next view,
  sort, search or circle change.
  *Prototype: round 1.*
- **Tapping into a note's text** starts editing it with the cursor where
  the user tapped, except on task checkboxes (they toggle; a long-press
  picks their state) and links
  (they open). Closed notes don't enter edit mode. *Prototype: round 2.*
- The editor renders Markdown live like Obsidian's mobile app: only the
  lines the cursor or selection touch stay raw; headings, emphasis,
  inline code, links, quotes, bullets and task checkboxes are rendered
  on all other lines, and checkboxes can be ticked while editing.
  *Prototype: round 2.*
- Lists continue on Enter (bullets, numbers, tasks as open tasks); Enter
  on an empty item ends the list. Bold / italic never wrap the list or
  heading marker. *Prototype: round 2.*
- The text is saved on every change. Editing ends with **Done**, `Esc`,
  the Android back button / gesture, or a tap anywhere outside the note
  and its toolbar; the tapped target then acts normally (e.g. starts
  editing that note). *Prototype: round 2; back button 2026-10-14.*
- A **toolbar** helps with typical actions (as in Obsidian): heading
  (cycles # → ## → ### → #### → none), bullet list, task checkbox, **task
  due date** (backlog #41, "Due date per task"), outdent /
  indent, bold, italic, **highlight**, link, **link to a note** (types the
  `[[` that opens the note picker, backlog #45), image or video (backlog #30),
  **counter**, **star rating**, undo / redo, and Done. No button for the
  note's due date and no microphone button (removed
  2026-10-16): the due date has its chip on the note, dictation the
  long-press on +. On phone and tablet it sits above the on-screen
  keyboard and scrolls sideways; on the desktop it floats at the bottom
  of the list. *Prototype: round 2.*
- **Highlight** (backlog #43, decided 2026-10-17): `==text==`
  (Obsidian's syntax) shows the text on a soft green (not yellow: that marks search hits), in the note and
  in the editor; the toolbar button wraps or unwraps the selection like
  bold. Other apps may show the `==` as text. *Prototype: 2026-10-17.*
- **Star rating** (backlog #42, decided 2026-10-17): three to ten stars,
  the filled ones first (`★★★☆☆`), are plain text and show as stars to
  tap, in the note and in the editor: a tap on the n-th star sets n, a
  tap on the highest filled star clears the rating; only the stars in
  the text change. The toolbar's star button inserts `☆☆☆☆☆` at the
  cursor. Not in closed, trashed or news notes. *Prototype: 2026-10-17.*
- **Tables** (backlog #44, decided 2026-10-17): Markdown tables show with
  lines, a header row and striped rows; a table wider than its note
  scrolls sideways inside it (the swipe between views leaves it alone),
  so cells keep their words whole on the phone. Written as plain
  Markdown, without editor help (backlog #54). *Prototype: 2026-10-17.*
- On the desktop the editor has shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+B bold, +I italic,
  +K link, +Enter tick / untick the task, Tab / Shift+Tab indent, Ctrl+Z
  / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo / redo. Outside the editor, `n` creates a note, `/`
  opens the search (Enter / Shift+Enter there step through the hits, ↓ / ↑
  and Enter pick a suggestion) and
  `Esc` ends editing or closes a panel.
  *Prototype: round 2.*

### Task states and progress

Decided 2026-10-16 (user request).

- A task has four states, plain Markdown as Obsidian themes write them:
  **open** `[ ]`, **done** `[x]`, **in progress** `[/]` (a half-filled
  box) and **cancelled** `[-]` (a struck box; its text faded and struck
  through like a done one). Why: in progress and cancelled are the two
  that are not just open or done; "deferred" stayed out, it reads like
  open.
- A **tap** on the box ticks it as before: open and in progress become
  done, done and cancelled become open. A **long-press** (desktop:
  right-click) opens a small menu with the four states, in the rendered
  note and in the editor; on the box it doesn't start multi-select.
  Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in the editor ticks like a tap; Enter after any task
  continues with an open one.
- **Done date**: ticking a task writes the day at the end of its line in
  the Obsidian Tasks syntax, `✅ YYYY-MM-DD` (after a due date;
  `docs/file-format.md`); unticking or another state removes it, setting
  done again keeps it. The app doesn't show it (rendered note, editor
  lines the cursor isn't on); it counts the task for the Due button's
  "done today" ring (decided 2026-10-18). Why in the file: it syncs, so
  every device counts the same; other editors show it as text.
- **Task progress** ("done/total") is shown when the switch next to the
  contents' − / + is on, and then both in the contents and at the
  notes' headings — nowhere else (user request). A heading counts its
  section's tasks with those under its subheadings; tasks before the
  first heading show in the note's meta line. Subtasks count, cancelled
  tasks don't count at all, in progress counts as open; a complete list
  shows green. The switch is a setting of this device, off by default,
  and remembered like the level count.
- **Clear done tasks** takes cancelled tasks along with the done ones;
  tasks in progress stay. A dated task goes like any other, its date with
  it (decided 2026-10-18).
- **Due date per task** (backlog #41, decided 2026-10-18): a task carries
  its own date in the Obsidian Tasks syntax, `📅 YYYY-MM-DD` at the end of
  its line (`docs/file-format.md`). The rendered note and the editor (on
  lines the cursor isn't on) show it as a chip in the due chip's look —
  red when overdue, accent-colored today; plain for a done or cancelled
  task and in the archive. A tap on the chip opens the **due-date menu**
  (as the note's: today, tomorrow, in a week, pick a date, remove) without
  entering edit mode. The editor toolbar's **Task due date** button
  (calendar) opens the same menu for the line the cursor is on, which
  becomes a task if it isn't one; typing the syntax works too. Why the
  toolbar: easiest to find, the same in all tiers, like counter and star
  rating; a "Due date…" entry in the task's long-press menu and typing
  only were tried and not chosen.
- **Task dates count for the note**: an open or in-progress task's date
  sorts the note by due date (the earliest of the note's own date and its
  tasks' dates), reminds on its day like a note's due date and shows in
  the Due view. The note's chip keeps showing only the note's own date,
  which stays a due date (backlog #65, decided 2026-10-18). Why: a dated
  task that neither sorts nor reminds would be decoration; every note is
  a to-do, so its date is a due date like a task's, and the Due view —
  not the chip — shows which task is due.

### Counters

- A **counter** is a number followed by its steps in square brackets,
  e.g. `P-2041 Website relaunch: 23,5 [-4 -1 +1 +8]` — for hour trackers,
  habits or anything counted. The steps are free per counter (each with a
  sign); decimals are allowed and keep the separator as written (`0,5` or
  `0.5`). Why: a counter stays plain Markdown that other apps show as
  text. *Prototype: 2026-10-16.*
- The rendered note and the live preview show the number as an accent
  chip; a tap pops its step buttons up around it, floating over the text
  (− steps left, + steps right, the number between them). The taps add
  up as a pending change shown next to the old number (`36 + 8` after
  two taps on `+4`); only closing them writes the sum into the number in
  the text, without entering edit mode. A tap beside them, `Esc` or the
  Android back key closes them (only them: an edit around them goes on)
  and every way of closing keeps the sum. Why: a double tap stays
  visible before it counts (user request 2026-10-16). Why: the note reads like
  plain text, the buttons appear where the user tapped (decided
  2026-10-16 over always visible buttons, a menu and a centered card).
  A tap on the number in the pop-up types an amount of one's own
  (without sign it adds, `-2` subtracts); it joins the pending change.
  When the on-screen keyboard comes up for it, the list scrolls the counter
  into the part left visible and the pop-up follows it, never behind the
  keyboard or the toolbar (found on Android 2026-10-19 with a counter low on
  the screen).
  Only the current value is kept, no history (the version history covers
  that). Archived, deleted and news notes show their counters read-only.
  Counters inside code are plain text.
- The toolbar's **counter** button adds `0 [-1 +1]` at the end of the
  current line (a line that has a counter stays as it is); the line then
  shows its Markdown to edit the steps. A long-press (desktop:
  right-click) on it adds a time counter with a stopwatch,
  `0:00 [-0:15 +0:15 ⏱15]`.
- **Times** (decided 2026-10-16, user request): a counter counts time in
  either of two forms — **hours and minutes** `3:45 [-0:15 +0:15]`
  (steps in h:mm too) or **decimal hours** with the unit `h`
  `23,5 h [-1 +1]`. Why: a plain `+1` doesn't say whether it means an
  hour or a minute. Typed into a time, a plain number is minutes (`40` →
  `+0:40`).
- A time counter can carry a **stopwatch** `⏱` in its brackets, a plain
  number can't (no unit). The number after it is the rounding in minutes
  (`⏱15`: quarter hours; `⏱` alone: to the minute); a run is always
  rounded **up**, at least one unit (usual for billed hours). Start and
  Stop are written at once (with any pending taps); while it runs, its
  start stands in the brackets, UTC to the second
  (`⏱15 2026-10-16T08:05:12Z`), so it runs on across devices and sync,
  and the chip shows the running time live. Start / Stop sits at the end
  of the pop-up's steps (decided 2026-10-16 over a second row and a
  Start / Stop part on the chip: a start or stop writes at once and rounds
  up, so it takes a deliberate second tap). Stopping adds the rounded
  run to the value. Several stopwatches may run at once. A running one
  can be **discarded** (✕ next to Stop): it stops without adding the run,
  e.g. when it was forgotten (user request) — the real time can then be
  typed in.
- **Running stopwatches show above the list** (user request), one chip
  each like an active filter, with the text before the counter on its
  line (else the note's title) and the running time — in every view and
  whatever the filters, so a forgotten one is seen. A tap opens the
  counter's pop-up right at the chip, with Stop and Discard.
  *Prototype: 2026-10-16.*

### Links between notes and private copies

Decided 2026-10-18 (backlog #45, user request).
